audit.process: Release / production deployment of billing-api + AI instrumentation (CLAUDE.md, release skill)

elements.finding: The three release preconditions (develop CI green, Flyway migrations aligned with prod, develop up to date) and the detection of success (grep SUCCESS/ERROR in the logs) live only in the prompt; the trigger of the prod deploy (step 4) has no human stopping point and no dry-run.
elements.target: Pure L2 skill: vocabulary, sequence `release plan` → human validation → `release run`, reading a JSON return (run url, conclusion), abort cases; the preconditions move down into the CLI subcommand `release plan` (exit 1) and into release.yml.
elements.check: SKILL.md no longer contains any manual check (Actions tab, prod dump, log grep); every step points to a subcommand or a workflow, and a step "ask for confirmation before `release run`" is explicit.

elements.finding: Mix of hardcoded L1 judgment (kind of version inferred from the branch name: develop = always minor, feat/breaking-* = major deployed to prod), L3 logic with no precondition and no test, and an immediate L4 trigger with no dry-run and no confirmation; VERSION is never incremented so the next release recomputes the same version and the tag push fails after overwriting the image.
elements.target: A tested CLI `release`: `release plan --type major|minor|patch [--dry-run]` (checks CI green, tree clean and up to date, tag does not exist, computes the version, outputs JSON) and `release run --plan <file>` (triggers the workflow, commits VERSION, returns the run URL); the kind of version is chosen by the human/agent (L1), not by the branch prefix.
elements.check: `release plan --type minor --dry-run` outputs JSON without triggering anything and exits with a code ≠ 0 if develop is red or behind; unit tests on the version computation and the preconditions; `scripts/release.mjs` removed.

elements.finding: workflow_dispatch that builds, publishes, tags and deploys to prod in a single job, with no protected `environment`, no `dry_run` input, no validation of the version format or of the tag, no concurrency, accepting any `ref`; the `hotfix` input is declared but never used; the success signal is an `echo SUCCESS`; `-Pversion` is overwritten by build.gradle, which re-reads VERSION.
elements.target: Two jobs: `publish` (regex validation x.y.z + tag does not exist, tests, bootJar, image, tag) then `deploy-prod` with `environment: production` and mandatory reviewers, a `dry_run` input that stops after the plan, `concurrency` per environment, explicit `permissions: contents: write`, structured outputs (version, image, run url) and removal of the `hotfix` input or a real use of it.
elements.check: A dispatch with `dry_run=true` touches neither the registry nor prod; a real dispatch stays waiting for approval on the `production` environment; a `version` that is not semver or already tagged makes the job fail before the build.

elements.finding: Dead script (the comment says so) but still executable: it builds, pushes and deploys to prod over SSH from a workstation, short-circuiting release.yml, the tests, the tag and any stopping point; no hook or settings.json prevents an agent from running it.
elements.target: Removed from the repository; the only path to prod is the `deploy-prod` job of release.yml.

elements.finding: Duplicates release.mjs (reading VERSION, parsing, computation, `gh workflow run`) with a single variation (patch); the `hotfix=true` input it passes is read nowhere in release.yml, so a hotfix is strictly identical to a release; same lack of dry-run and of confirmation.
elements.target: Absorbed by `release plan --type patch`; the check "starts from a hotfix/* branch" becomes a precondition of the CLI when `--type patch` is asked outside a prod tag.
elements.check: `scripts/hotfix.mjs` removed; SKILL.md no longer mentions it; `release plan --type patch` fails (exit ≠ 0) outside a hotfix/* or release/* branch.

elements.finding: Mix of instruction (29 %), reference (45 %) and noise (26 %); the "well-formed service" example uses the field injection that the rule just above forbids (and the real code copies it); the "Release process" section duplicates SKILL.md with the same grep of SUCCESS; dead references (InvoiceServiceTest, docker compose, packages customer/payment/config/security, dto folder); no maintenance clause.
elements.target: A short CLAUDE.md (≈40 lines): rules with their why and the guardrail that carries them, working process, a pointer to the release skill; reference (commands, troubleshooting, stack) moved out into `docs/` loaded on demand; example fixed to constructor injection; clause "any rule added in review goes into this file in the same PR, any rule with no violation for 6 months is removed".
elements.check: Service example complying with the rule it illustrates; no command or path cited is absent from the repository; Release section reduced to one line pointing to `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md`; share of reference < 30 %.

elements.finding: Healthy L4 gate: Checkstyle main+test and test suite (ArchUnit included) on push to develop/main and on PRs; it is the guardrail of "run the full suite before a PR".
elements.target: Unchanged; its result becomes the source read by `release plan` (conclusion of the last run on develop).
elements.check: `release plan` reads the conclusion of ci.yml via `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch develop --json conclusion`.

elements.finding: Carries four rules of CLAUDE.md (length 120, no import *, one public class per file, naming of constants/methods); desirable P3 extension: ImportOrder/CustomImportOrder, TypeName, MemberName to cover the rest of the Naming/Code Style section.
elements.target: Unchanged in its role; the missing modules added so that the Code Style section of CLAUDE.md becomes a one-line pointer.
elements.check: An import not grouped java/javax/org/com or a class in camelCase makes `./gradlew checkstyleMain` fail.

elements.finding: Exemplary guardrail of "no repository in controllers": the javadoc cites the CLAUDE.md rule it carries; it is the right place to host the rule "constructor injection" and "no @MockBean in a unit test".
elements.target: Unchanged; hosts the new ArchUnit rules coming from the PUSH_DOWN of CLAUDE.md.
elements.check: Each ArchUnit rule cites the CLAUDE.md line it guards, and each mandatory rule of CLAUDE.md points to its test.

elements.finding: Wires Checkstyle and ArchUnit and makes VERSION the source of truth of the version; this assignment overwrites the `-Pversion` passed by release.yml, an inconsistency to resolve on the workflow/CLI side (commit VERSION) rather than here.
elements.target: Unchanged; the CLI `release run` commits VERSION on the ref before triggering the workflow, and release.yml stops passing `-Pversion`.
elements.check: The jar produced by release.yml carries the tagged version (`ls build/libs` in the job).

process_leaks.rule: Never release if the CI of develop is not green
process_leaks.if_skipped: An image built on a red develop (tests or Checkstyle failing) goes to prod: release.yml does not re-run the tests and does not read the status of ci.yml
process_leaks.guard_tool: Subcommand `release plan`: `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch develop --json conclusion` → exit 1 if ≠ success; doubled by a `./gradlew test` step in the publish job of release.yml (L4)

process_leaks.rule: Check that no Flyway migration is left unapplied in prod before releasing
process_leaks.if_skipped: Unexpected migration or FlywayValidateException when the container starts in prod, discovered after `docker compose up -d`; the step also asks the owner for a dump of the prod database
process_leaks.guard_tool: `flyway info`/`flyway validate` step (or `./gradlew flywayInfo`) against the prod database in the deploy-prod job, before the `docker pull`, with exit ≠ 0 on an unexpected state

process_leaks.rule: Be on an up-to-date develop (checkout + pull) before running the release
process_leaks.if_skipped: release.mjs checks only the name of the branch: a local develop that is behind or a dirty tree produces a `ref` and a VERSION that do not match what will be deployed
process_leaks.guard_tool: `release plan`: `git fetch` then exit 1 if `git status -sb` shows behind/ahead or a tree that is not clean

process_leaks.rule: The release succeeded when the output of the workflow contains SUCCESS; on ERROR/FAILED warn and do not run again
process_leaks.if_skipped: Hallucinated or missed success: `gh workflow run` returns no run id, the SUCCESS is a plain `echo` (release.yml:32) and a partly failed run (image pushed, tag failed) cannot be told apart
process_leaks.guard_tool: `release run` returns the run URL and waits for `gh run view <id> --json conclusion,jobs`; release.yml exposes outputs (version, image, step reached)

process_leaks.rule: Human stopping point between the release plan and the deployment to production
process_leaks.if_skipped: An agent or a `node scripts/release.mjs` run by mistake deploys to prod with no dry-run and no validation; no protection on the workflow side
process_leaks.guard_tool: `environment: production` with required reviewers on the deploy-prod job + `dry_run` input; on the L3 side, `release plan --dry-run` by default and `release run` that requires the plan

process_leaks.if_skipped: Hidden dependencies, services that cannot be unit-tested; already broken by InvoiceService.java:10 and by the example of CLAUDE.md:74

process_leaks.rule: Every endpoint has an authorization test (wrong role → 403)
process_leaks.if_skipped: A billing endpoint exposed with no role check passes CI; InvoiceControllerTest.java:8 records that no 403 test exists
process_leaks.guard_tool: JUnit test parameterised on `RequestMappingHandlerMapping`: for each mapping, a request with `@WithMockUser(roles="NONE")` must answer 401/403; fails when an endpoint is added without a security rule

process_leaks.rule: Never modify a Flyway migration already applied
process_leaks.if_skipped: Detected only at startup in prod (FlywayValidateException, CLAUDE.md:104), that is, after the deployment
process_leaks.guard_tool: CI check as a PR gate: `migrations check` script comparing the checksums of `src/main/resources/db/migration/V*` with the target branch (`git diff --name-status origin/develop -- db/migration` → exit 1 on M/D), or a Testcontainers test `flyway migrate` + `validate`

guarded_rules.rule: No business logic and no repository access in controllers
Constants in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, methods in camelCase (partial: no TypeName/MemberName)
Full suite + Checkstyle before any PR / on every push
A hotfix starts from a hotfix/* branch
A release starts from develop, release/* or feat/breaking-* (debatable scope)

remediation.action: Remove scripts/old-deploy.sh (or at least drop the executable bit and move it out of the repository); no other SSH path to prod.acme.io outside release.yml.
remediation.check: The file is absent; `grep -r prod.acme.io` returns only release.yml.

remediation.action: Rework release.yml: jobs `publish` and `deploy-prod` (environment: production, required reviewers), `dry_run` input, regex validation x.y.z + `git ls-remote --tags` empty, `./gradlew test` step, `concurrency: release-prod`, `permissions: contents: write`, outputs version/image/run, removal of the unused `hotfix` input and of the `echo SUCCESS`, `-Pversion` dropped in favour of the committed VERSION file.
remediation.check: Dispatch `dry_run=true`: no registry push, no ssh; real dispatch: deploy-prod job waiting for approval; version `abc` or already tagged: failure before the build.

remediation.action: Create a tested CLI (e.g. `tools/release/` or `npm run release -- plan|run`): `plan --type major|minor|patch [--dry-run]` checks CI green, tree clean/up to date, tag does not exist, computes the version and writes a JSON plan; `run --plan` bumps + commits VERSION, triggers release.yml and returns the run URL + conclusion; unit tests of the version computation and of the preconditions.
remediation.check: `plan --dry-run` triggers nothing and exits 1 on a develop that is red/behind; `run` refuses without a plan; tests green in CI.

remediation.action: Remove scripts/release.mjs and scripts/hotfix.mjs once the CLI is in place; the hotfix case becomes `plan --type patch` with the precondition "hotfix/* or release/* branch".
remediation.check: Both .mjs are absent; `plan --type patch` outside hotfix/* exits with a code ≠ 0.

remediation.action: Rewrite SKILL.md: sequence `plan` → show the JSON plan to the human and wait for their agreement → `run` → read `conclusion`; keep the abort cases (failure = warn, do not run again) and the #releases announcement; drop the Actions tab, the prod dump and the SUCCESS/ERROR grep.
remediation.check: No manual check and no log reading in SKILL.md; an explicit confirmation step comes before `run`.

remediation.action: Add to ArchitectureTest the rule `noFields().should().beAnnotatedWith(Autowired.class)` and fix InvoiceService.java to constructor injection; fix the example CLAUDE.md:70-81.
remediation.check: `./gradlew test --tests ArchitectureTest` fails if an `@Autowired` is put back on a field; the example of CLAUDE.md complies with the rule.

remediation.action: Add a generic authorization test (iteration over RequestMappingHandlerMapping, `@WithMockUser(roles="NONE")` → 401/403) and an explicit Spring Security configuration; replace CLAUDE.md:57 with a pointer to this test.
remediation.check: Adding a `@GetMapping` without a security rule makes CI fail.

remediation.action: Add a CI step "immutable migrations" (diff of the `db/migration/V*` files modified/deleted against the target branch → exit 1) or a Testcontainers test `flyway validate`; CLAUDE.md:63 points to this gate.
remediation.check: A PR that modifies V1__init.sql is red in CI.

remediation.action: Reduce CLAUDE.md to ≈40 lines: rules + why + guardrail, working process (when to stop, criterion of done), one line pointing to the release skill; move Build/Stack/Troubleshooting/Package structure out into `docs/dev.md`; remove the dead references (InvoiceServiceTest, docker compose, packages that do not exist, dto folder); add the maintenance clause.
remediation.check: Every command and path cited exists; share of reference < 30 %; maintenance clause present; Release section = 1 line.

remediation.action: Add CustomImportOrder (java/javax/org/com), TypeName, MemberName, ParameterName; remove lines 65-66 and 85 from CLAUDE.md in favour of a pointer "Checkstyle is authoritative".
remediation.check: `./gradlew checkstyleMain` fails on a badly grouped import or a badly named class.

remediation.action: Add `gh release create v${version} --generate-notes` to the publish job so that the "list of PRs included" (SKILL.md:22) is produced by L4 and not rebuilt by the agent.
remediation.check: Every tag has a GitHub Release with generated notes; the skill points to its URL for the announcement.
